replacements.before: Actor and Human Approval fields (enhancement only): for proposal preparer, one-time initial applier [identity/environment/one-time scope], verifier, and reviewer, record the role/Agent definition repository-relative path and content SHA-256, each bound to that actor's own unique attempt record; record current runtime identity/environment separately. Check distinctness using the actor-identity bindings, not display name alone. Different OS identities, hosts, or repositories are not required unless an applicable, explicitly approved security boundary requires them. Qualification evidence [record path/ID/SHA-256 and capability observations]; approval decision/source/time; approved report fingerprint and exact targets. Each Application, Verification, Review, and Audit request must separately record its fresh attributable stage-start instruction; this is not part of or a substitute for patch approval.
replacements.after: Actor and Human Approval fields (enhancement only; stage-specific): record the proposal preparer, intended one-time initial applier [identity/environment/one-time scope], intended verifier, and intended reviewer by role/Agent definition repository-relative path and content SHA-256. At proposal preparation, bind only the actual preparer to its own current unique attempt and record its current runtime identity/environment and qualification evidence [record path/ID/SHA-256 and capability observations] separately. The intended applier requires fresh exact Human Approval and one-time designation; no separate pre-existing qualification attempt is required. After its separate fresh Application stage-start, the applier must publish and integrity-check its own current attempt, identity, permissions, and role-specific capability evidence before any source write; before Application source work, both preparer and applier must be bound to their own attempts. Record future verifier/reviewer bindings as planned identity-only paths and hashes, not attempts, current runtime identities, capabilities, or stage starts; do not require, create, or publish their attempts before predecessor gates. Only after complete successful Application and a fresh Verification stage-start may the actual verifier publish its own attempt and current qualification; only after passing independent Verification and a fresh Review stage-start may the actual reviewer do so. Each actual verifier/reviewer definition path and hash must match its approved planned binding; mismatch blocks that stage pending updated attributable Human decision and exact approval. Follow the Governance Amendment Application controls for these bindings and gates. Check all four actors' distinctness using actor-identity bindings, not display name alone; the applier must also differ from the SDLC Process Orchestrator and any Governance Remediation actor barred from self-edit in its active cycle. Different OS identities, hosts, or repositories are not required unless an applicable, explicitly approved security boundary requires them. Record the approval decision/source/time, approved report fingerprint, and exact targets without treating approval/designation as capability evidence. Each Application, Verification, Review, and Audit request must separately record its fresh attributable stage-start instruction and each actual actor must qualify in its own current invocation under SDLC_ARTIFACT_GOVERNANCE.md section 33.1; stage-start is not part of or a substitute for patch approval.

approval_route: Fresh exact Human Approval and fresh explicit one-time applier designation may be combined in one attributable decision. Neither is supplied. Every later process needs its own fresh start; no pre-existing applier qualification record or future assurance attempt is required.
byte_contract: Exact sequential replacements and byte/hash fields are binding; unified diff is the corresponding minimal presentation patch. All target UTF-8/CRLF/BOM/final-newline properties preserved.
